feature1.prompt: LassoLarsIC: unintuitive copy_X behaviour. The LassoLarsIC class currently has a conflicting implementation regarding the copy_X parameter: it is specified both during instance initialization and again in the fit method, which results in the instance-level setting being silently overwritten by the fit method's default value. When a user sets copy_X to a specific value at creation (for example, copy_X=False) and later calls fit without explicitly providing a value, the intended behavior is lost. The goal is to modify the fit method so that if no explicit copy_X is provided, the setting from the instance is used. This change will enforce a clear and consistent behavior for copy_X across the class.
feature1.hint_texts: Modify the LassoLarsIC.fit method by changing its signature to set the default of copy_X to None instead of True. Add a conditional check that, if copy_X is None, assigns it the value of the instance attribute (self.copy_X). Ensure that if a value is explicitly passed to fit, it overrides the instance setting. This update should maintain compatibility with unrelated behaviors of the class.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sklearn/linear_model/least_angle.py; Function: fit (around lines 1479-1500), where the copy_X parameter and its handling are modified.

feature2.prompt: LassoLarsIC: unintuitive copy_X behaviour. The inconsistency arises because the copy_X parameter is provided in two places: at initialization and in the fit method. This dual source creates an unexpected override where the value set during instance creation is replaced by the default value in fit when no explicit argument is provided. The desired behavior is that the instance-level copy_X setting should be preserved when fit is called without an override, while an explicit copy_X passed to fit should take precedence. This distinction will make the parameter behavior intuitive and predictable for users.
feature2.hint_texts: Develop new test cases to verify the intuitive behavior of the copy_X parameter. Create tests that instantiate LassoLarsIC with a specific copy_X value and call fit without an explicit copy_X to confirm that the instance value is used. Additionally, write tests that pass an explicit copy_X value to the fit method to ensure it overrides the instance-level setting. Place these tests in the appropriate test file to validate both scenarios.
feature2.entrypoint: File: sklearn/linear_model/tests/test_least_angle.py; New test functions to add: test_lasso_lars_copyX_behaviour and test_lasso_lars_fit_copyX_behaviour.
